sections.skill: Spot exposed secrets and unsafe handling of input

questions.prompt: What is an API key?

choices.text: A keyboard key that programmers press to run their code faster than usual
A code that lets a program use a private or paid service

questions.correct_answer: A code that lets a program use a private or paid service
questions.intro: A SECRET is a password, API key (a code that lets a program use a paid or private service) or similar credential. Never write secrets directly in code that will be shared or committed; store them separately, for example in a settings file kept private or an ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE (a value set outside the code). Also never paste secrets into a chat with an AI tool. A second risk is UNSAFE INPUT: code that takes what a user types and builds a command from it can be tricked. SQL (Structured Query Language) for databases is a classic case: inserting typed text straight into a query lets attackers change the query.

sections.skill: Compare secrets in code with a house key under the doormat

questions.prompt: Why is a key under the doormat risky?

choices.text: Because doormats damage keys over time, making them stop working in the lock
Anyone who looks can find it

questions.correct_answer: Anyone who looks can find it
questions.intro: Leaving a house key under the doormat is convenient, but anyone who looks there can get in. Writing a password or API key directly in code is similar: anyone who sees the code, or a copy of it, can use the key. Keeping the key in your pocket, separate from the house, is like storing secrets outside the code. And if the key might have been copied, you change the lock rather than just moving the key.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Respond to exposed secrets and untrusted input

questions.prompt: Why is deleting an exposed key from the code not enough?

choices.text: Because deleting lines of code in a file is impossible once the file has been shared
It may already have been copied

questions.correct_answer: It may already have been copied
questions.intro: Generated code often uses placeholder secrets ("API_KEY = 'your-key-here'"), and people replace them with real keys in the same spot, then share the file. If a secret is exposed, CHANGE IT (rotate it) at the service right away; deleting it from the code is not enough. For input, use the safe methods a language provides, such as PARAMETERIZED QUERIES that keep user text separate from the command, and treat everything a user types as untrusted.

questions.prompt: What does "rotate a secret" mean?

choices.text: Move the secret to a different line of the same code file so it is harder to find
